config.title: Session Timeout Hook

intro.title: Session Timeout Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useSessionTimeout` that automatically logs a user out after a period of inactivity. You will learn how to use the `useState` and `useEffect` hooks to manage state and side effects, and how to handle browser events like mouse movements and key presses. The main technologies involved are React hooks and JavaScript event listeners. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that can help secure applications by managing user sessions.
intro.usecase: Session timeout hooks are essential in secure applications where user inactivity could compromise data. In banking dashboards, they automatically log users out after periods of inactivity to prevent unauthorized access to financial information. E-commerce checkout forms use them to expire sessions and clear cart data when users abandon the process. Admin panels implement these hooks to protect sensitive configuration interfaces from being left open on shared computers. Developers add these hooks to comply with security standards while maintaining user experience through clear timeout warnings.

objectives: Construct a custom React hook to manage session timeout logic
Initialize state variables to track user activity and remaining time
Implement event listeners to detect user interactions and reset the timer
Configure a countdown mechanism that updates the remaining time display
Integrate the session timeout hook into a functional React component
Render visual feedback based on the session timeout state (active, warning, expired)
Manipulate the DOM to show/hide timeout warnings and session expiration messages

steps.title: Import React and all hooks needed for this lesson (useState, useEffect, useRef, useCallback)
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useEffect, useRef, and useCallback from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all the required hooks from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple hooks from React
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef, useCallback } from 'react';

steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and the useState, useEffect, useRef, and useCallback hooks are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React, useState, useEffect, useRef, and useCallback are all imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but you need to import all five items: React, useState, useEffect, useRef, and useCallback from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's start with the basics. We need to import React and the specific hooks we'll use throughout this lesson. Try importing React, useState, useEffect, useRef, and useCallback from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the useSessionTimeout custom hook
steps.instruction: Create a function called useSessionTimeout that takes timeoutDuration and onTimeout as parameters. The function should be empty for now.
steps.hint: Define a function with the given name and parameters. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef, useCallback } from 'react';

// Create the useSessionTimeout custom hook here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named useSessionTimeout is defined with two parameters: timeoutDuration and onTimeout.
successCriteria: The code contains a function named useSessionTimeout that accepts timeoutDuration and onTimeout as parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is named exactly 'useSessionTimeout' and accepts both timeoutDuration and onTimeout parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that you used the exact name 'useSessionTimeout' and included both parameters.

steps.title: Initialize state for tracking remaining time
steps.instruction: Inside the useSessionTimeout hook, use the useState hook to create a state variable called remainingTime, initialized to the timeoutDuration parameter.
steps.hint: Remember to destructure useState from React and call it with the initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for a countdown
const [timeLeft, setTimeLeft] = useState(initialTime);
steps.expectedOutcome: The useSessionTimeout hook will have a remainingTime state variable initialized with the timeoutDuration value.
successCriteria: The useSessionTimeout hook contains a useState call that creates a remainingTime state variable initialized to timeoutDuration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've correctly initialized the state variable. Make sure you're using useState and setting the initial value to timeoutDuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The remainingTime state hasn't been properly initialized. Remember to use useState inside the hook to create this state variable.

steps.title: Define the resetTimer function
steps.instruction: Inside the useSessionTimeout hook, create a function named resetTimer that sets remainingTime back to timeoutDuration.
steps.hint: The resetTimer function should update the remainingTime state using the setRemainingTime setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The resetTimer function will allow resetting the session countdown when user activity is detected.
successCriteria: A resetTimer function is defined that calls setRemainingTime with timeoutDuration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure resetTimer calls setRemainingTime with timeoutDuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The resetTimer function should update the remainingTime state back to the original timeoutDuration.

steps.title: Wrap resetTimer with useCallback
steps.instruction: Wrap the resetTimer function with useCallback to maintain a stable reference across renders.
steps.hint: Use the useCallback hook to memoize the resetTimer function. Pass an empty dependency array to ensure it's only created once.
steps.expectedOutcome: The resetTimer function is wrapped with useCallback, preventing unnecessary recreations on each render.
successCriteria: useCallback has an empty dependency array
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useCallback correctly. Check that you've wrapped the entire resetTimer function and provided an empty dependency array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The resetTimer function needs to be wrapped with useCallback. Remember to import useCallback from 'react' and use it to memoize the function.

steps.title: Add timeout detection and cleanup
steps.instruction: Inside the same useEffect, add logic to call onTimeout when remainingTime reaches 0, and return a cleanup function that clears the interval.
steps.hint: Use an if statement to check if remainingTime is 0, then call onTimeout. Return a function that clears the interval stored in timerRef.current.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect will now detect when the timer reaches zero and clean up the interval properly.
successCriteria: An if statement checks if remainingTime is 0 and calls onTimeout
A cleanup function is returned that clears timerRef.current
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both the timeout detection (if remainingTime === 0) and the cleanup function that clears the interval.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding timeout detection and cleanup inside the useEffect. Check the hint and analogous example for guidance.

steps.title: Use the custom hook in App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, call the useSessionTimeout hook with a 10-second timeout duration and pass a timeout handler function that logs 'Session timed out!' to the console.
steps.hint: Call the hook at the top of the App component function body, providing the timeout duration in milliseconds and a callback function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will call the custom hook with a 10-second duration and a handler function that logs a message when the timeout occurs.
successCriteria: useSessionTimeout is called inside App with 10000 as the timeout duration and a function that logs 'Session timed out!' to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current remaining time in seconds.
steps.hint: Use the remainingTime value from the hook's return value in a JSX expression.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will display the remaining time in seconds below the heading.
successCriteria: A paragraph element shows the remaining time value from the hook.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The timer display is now visible in the UI.

steps.title: Add reset button and wire it to resetTimer
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's JSX, add a button element with the text 'Reset Timer' and wire its onClick event to call the resetTimer function from the hook.
steps.hint: Place the button after the timer display paragraph. Use onClick={resetTimer} to connect the button click to the reset function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an interactive button
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will include a functional reset button that, when clicked, resets the session timer by calling the resetTimer function.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Reset Timer' is added to the JSX, and its onClick prop is set to call the resetTimer function.
